subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should trusted plugins be allowed to synchronously inspect and veto every canonical configuration write, and under what redaction, failure, timeout, and recovery contract?
rationale: This changes the Plugin SDK and makes plugin execution part of a security- and availability-sensitive persistence boundary; source inspection cannot determine the intended trust and fail-open/fail-closed policy.

options.title: Add a bounded trusted-plugin veto
options.body: Expose a typed, redacted pre-persistence event from the canonical writer with strict timeout, rejection, recursion, and operator-recovery semantics.

options.title: Keep validation core-owned
options.body: Do not expose a veto hook; instead extend built-in validation and doctor rules for configuration invariants that OpenClaw officially supports.

options.title: Offer advisory validation only
options.body: Let plugins report diagnostics before writes while core validation remains the only blocking authority.

recommendation.title: Add a bounded trusted-plugin veto
recommendation.body: Expose a typed, redacted pre-persistence event from the canonical writer with strict timeout, rejection, recursion, and operator-recovery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing issue review already routes this gap into configuration mutation product direction and distinguishes it from current built-in safeguards.
